answer: A reef of shared, stake-backed reputation works like a garden that only grows for agents who keep tending it: each new agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete verifiable work before it can transact. An isolated island account with no history or stake cannot flood the market, because creating many fake identities means locking a deposit for each one and risking forfeiture if any of them misbehaves. Sybil attackers then pay linearly per identity while honest agents reuse one established, costly-to-build reputation.
